concepts.title: What Economics Studies: The Ordinary Business of Life
concepts.definition: Economics, as Alfred Marshall put it, studies man in the ordinary business of life -- how people earn, spend, save and choose among scarce means. Scarcity and choice form its core: unlimited wants chasing limited resources force every household, firm and government to economise.
concepts.key_idea: Unlimited wants, limited resources -- every economic act is a choice about scarcity.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest101.txt opening sections (alfred marshall definition, ordinary business of life, scarcity and choice, consumers and producers)
question_patterns: state alfred marshall's definition of economics
in class 11 introduction to statistics for economics: why is economics called the study of the ordinary business of life
explain scarcity and choice with an example
what economic activities do consumers and producers perform
why must every economy choose what how and for whom to produce
distinguish economic from non economic activities

solution_steps.explain: Marshall's definition places economics inside daily life -- earning, spending, saving.
Wants multiply while resources stay limited, so scarcity forces choice at every level.
Households consume, firms produce, and governments provision -- the ordinary business economics studies.

concepts.title: Why Economics Needs Statistics
concepts.definition: Economic facts come as numbers -- prices, incomes, output, employment -- and statistics is the tool-set that collects, organises, presents, analyses and interprets them. Without statistical methods, the economist's statements would remain vague impressions instead of tested conclusions.
concepts.key_idea: Economics thinks in numbers -- statistics turns those numbers into evidence.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest101.txt statistics sections (role of statistics in economics, statistical tools, data as numerical statements, use in policy)
question_patterns: what is statistics in the plural and singular sense
in class 11 introduction: why does economics need statistics
list the stages of a statistical study
give examples of statistical data used in economics
how does statistics help government policy
can economic statements be made without numbers discuss

solution_steps.explain: Statistics means both numerical data and the methods of handling such data.
Collection, organisation, presentation, analysis and interpretation form the pipeline every study follows.
Quantified evidence turns economic guesses into tested findings for households, firms and governments.

concepts.title: The Three Central Problems of an Economy
concepts.definition: Every economy, rich or poor, must answer three questions: what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce. Market economies answer through prices; centrally planned economies through state decisions; mixed economies blend both -- and statistics measures how well each answer works.
concepts.key_idea: What, how, for whom -- three questions every economy must answer, by market or by plan.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest101.txt problems sections (what how and for whom, market economy, planned economy, mixed economy)
question_patterns: state the three central problems of an economy
in class 11 introduction: how does a market economy answer what to produce
why does scarcity create the problem of choice of technique
for whom to produce is decided by what mechanism explain
relate the central problems to your household's budget decisions

solution_steps.explain: With scarce resources, choosing which goods to make means refusing others -- the what problem.
Labour-intensive or capital-intensive technique is a cost-and-availability choice -- the how problem.
Distribution of output across households completes the trio -- the for whom problem.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A minister claims inflation is falling. Explain the role statistics must play before the claim is believed.

solution_template.explain: Price data must be collected systematically from markets over comparable periods.
The data are organised, presented and analysed -- an index computed -- before interpretation.
Only the statistical pipeline converts a claim about inflation into tested evidence.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A state must choose between building a hospital and a highway. Explain which central problem this illustrates and how the choice is made.

solution_template.explain: Choosing between two uses of scarce public funds is the 'what to produce' problem.
In a mixed economy the government decides through planning, budgets and appraisal of needs.
Data on health indicators and traffic support the choice -- statistics informing the economic decision.
